fields.source_first_note: Read the complete623-character Hindi field. The route relays Ibn Abbas from the source-named Saab ibn Jathama, who offers the wild-ass gift; the Prophet returns it and explains only the ihram reason after seeing grief on his face. Keep both Abwa/Waddan alternatives and the explicit unnamed-transmitter location uncertainty: it materially qualifies the event location and is not Prophet speech. The bracketed grief-signs object supplies the observed reaction triggering the explanation and remains. The English wild donkey parenthesis is a dictionary gloss and stays context; the long prefatory route is context while source attribution remains metadata. No missing locality or narrator certainty is supplied.

Read all535 Urdu characters independently. Ibn Abbas/Saab attribution is supplied by the prefatory route; the own body reports the gift, location Abwa or Waddan, refusal and ihram explanation. Preserve the exact double aur spelling, the location alternatives and unnamed narrator uncertainty as a qualified transmission statement in the same family, not Prophet words. Ranj ke asar fills the actual seen reaction on the gift-giver face; retain it. Separate the multistep route only, leaving names available in complete source context and metadata. There is no English gloss in this field and none is imported.

Read all448 Hindi characters. Aisha reports that people waited for her turn to send gifts to the Prophet, seeking his pleasure by gifts or by that particular-day wait. The recipient-in-service parenthesis supplies actual object/recipient scope and remains. The two alternatives and printed unnamed narrator doubt materially qualify which motivation/action wording is transmitted; retain that qualification separately from Aisha account and never label it Prophet speech. The opening multistep route is context. Preserve the actual distinction between gift and day, rather than silently settling either.

Read all407 Urdu characters independently. The supplied Aisha report describes gifts, her turn and the aim of the Prophet happiness. Keep the explicit recipient clause and both gift-versus-particular-day alternatives; narrator doubt qualifies that material alternative and belongs to an unnamed transmission voice, not Prophet speech. Context begins with the pure prefatory transmitter route. The own words give finite habitual action, not merely a reference or compiler instruction.

Read the entire667-character Hindi field. Ibn Abbas reports aunt Umm Hufayd gifts of cheese, ghee and lizard, the Prophet eating the first two and leaving the disliked lizard. His later explicit statement that it was eaten at the Prophet table and could not have been so eaten if forbidden is an actual Companion argument, not compiler legal explanation or Prophet speech; make that a distinct component in the same food-event family. Separate the prefatory route and both sahna dictionary synonyms. The printed isi same-table link belongs to the domain of Ibn Abbas stated inference and may remain. Preserve the dislike reason and conditional inference exactly; no independent law or authenticity conclusion is supplied.

Read all599 Urdu characters. The body supplies Ibn Abbas report of his aunt gifts, the Prophet eating cheese/ghee and leaving the lizard because of dislike, then Ibn Abbas own table-based conditional argument. Distinguish this actual Companion saying from the reported Prophet conduct in one family. The two sahna parentheses are lexical synonyms and context; the pure prefatory chain is context. Keep the same-table link and conditional if-forbidden wording because they delimit the speaker evidence and inference. Do not convert his source statement into a new general ruling or Prophet quotation.
